systems.name: creative-apps
systems.description: SuiteUI's slice of creative-apps, as planned in docs/blueprints/suiteui.md section 2. Same shape as docs/c4/model.json, with status (planned or existing) and authored on every container and component. Planning only: the C4 gate reads docs/c4/model.json, not this file.

containers.name: SuiteUI
containers.description: The shared design system and component library (Sources/SuiteUI). Knows no Model and no engine. macOS only today.

components.name: Tokens and glass
components.description: Spacing, insets, radii, sizes, type, motion and the color tokens (graphite ladder, text and state colors as literal hex per appearance, Increase Contrast included); Liquid Glass applied in one snapshot-aware place (suiteGlass(in:)) and GlassPanel. The only place a raw value or a material may appear (design lint).

components.name: Window shell
components.description: SuiteWindow: the split-view window (sidebar of SidebarSections, content, hideable inspector) with launch and minimum sizes derived from the column tokens. Planned: the -SuiteGallery launch hook that shows SuiteGallery instead of the app's content (suite-harness), app-owned expansion and row context menus (lists).

components.name: Editor shell
components.description: EditorShell (top bar, docked rail, canvas, right panel, status line; dark in both appearances; planned: the resizable, collapsible timeline slot), EditorTopBar with EditorBarItem, EditorBarMenu and EditorBarDivider (planned: outlined items, one .primary, the save status), SegmentedTabs (planned: capsule look), and ShellLayout (planned, pure): column widths at a window width and the timeline slot's clamped height and collapse.

components.name: Tool palette
components.description: ToolbarAction (title, symbol, selected, unavailableHelp, one-key shortcut, handler), PaletteTool and ToolbarGroup in the floating glass and docked rail styles. An action can only be disabled by saying why. Planned: rail colors (#341).

components.name: Canvas
components.description: CanvasSurface (artboard centered over the surround) and CanvasViewport (checkerboard, rulers, zoom 10 to 3200 percent, Space-drag and arrow pan, drags in document pixels, onDragEnd once per gesture), Ruler with RulerTicks, ZoomMath. Planned: the ruler corner unit (#264).

components.name: Canvas marks
components.description: Marks drawn over document content in a CanvasViewport overlay, never hit-tested themselves: SelectionOutline and CropShade (existing); planned: SelectionHandles (eight handles and the rotate zone, hit size fixed in view points at any zoom), PathMarks, MotionPathMarks, GhostLayer, guide marks (#273), CanvasPointMark (#706, #737) and CanvasGrid (#530), with HandleGeometry, the pure handle layout, hit and resize math.

components.name: Inspector rows
components.description: InspectorHeader (title and info card), InspectorSection (caps header, collapse, Reset; planned: a 20 pt Reset hit beside the header button, #622 #285), InspectorRow, InspectorSliderRow, InspectorStepperRow, InspectorPickerRow, the one color row (HexColor, InspectorColorRow, InspectorColorWellRow; planned: onEnd, #718), InspectorAction and KeyframeButton with KeyState.

components.name: Number entry
components.description: ScrubField (exact number) and the bar slider look, ScrubValue (drag, step, snap, fill, defaults; ScrubTrack for non-linear tracks; ViewerZoom), NumericInput (parse, format, spoken text) and StudioScrubRow. Planned: public onEnd on the exact field (#718), a track-owned discrete step (#591), readable accessibility values (#262).

components.name: Presets and chips
components.description: SuiteChipStyle, PresetGrid (one on at most, arrow keys move focus), ChoiceChips (three columns) and ChipRow (toggle chips that report On or Off).

components.name: Curve editors
components.description: CurveEditor (two-handle easing well, preview dot hidden under Reduce Motion, nudges, Tab between handles, one onEnd per gesture) and ToneCurveEditor (N points over a histogram; add, move, remove, nudge). Planned: goldens and the Reduce Motion probe mark (#343).

components.name: Rows and lists
components.description: SidebarItem, SidebarToggle and SidebarRow (row toggles in one column, rename draft), SidebarSection and SidebarNode (two-level cap). Planned: LayerList, the panel container for layers and scenes outside a split view, with dimmed rows (#146), keyboard rename and a refusable rename that keeps the draft (#108, #577), reorder, row context menus (#73), separately reachable child-row toggles (#589), app-owned expansion (#111), and ListEditing, the pure rename and reorder rules.

components.name: Thumbnail grid
components.description: ThumbnailItem, ThumbnailBadges and ThumbnailGrid (adaptive columns, click, Shift, Command and arrow selection) with GridSelection, its pure selection math.

components.name: Timeline
components.description: TimelineTrack and TimelineStrip (names column, ruler, one lane per track with key diamonds and spans) with FrameMapping (frame to x and back, ruler marks, key hit-testing). Planned: the restyle with lane beds, name chips, key states, the playhead pill and the recording ring (#62), and TimelineKeys, the pure key selection and drag rules (#63).

components.name: Viewer chrome
components.description: ViewerStatusBar (facts as status pills; toggle and warning pill styles) and, planned, TransportCapsule (start, step back, play and pause, step forward, end, loop, with the timecode readout) (#340).

components.name: Content surfaces
components.description: SurfaceCard and EmptyStateView (ContentUnavailableView with the one prominent action; planned: the primary button style, #339).

components.name: Node graph
components.description: NodeGraph: nodes drawn at the positions the app gives, arrows that meet node edges with condition chips, a self-loop, warning badges, the active node highlighted (#344); NodeGraphGeometry holds the pure arrow and loop geometry.

components.name: Probes
components.description: FrameProbe: input-to-display timings in frames late, dropped frames, tick jitter and in-app marks, exposed as the suite.perf accessibility value only under the perf launch flag (#330). ControlInventory: every SuiteUI control registers its identifier, enabled state and reason, exposed as suite.controls under the same flag, for every app's every-control sweep.

components.name: Component gallery
components.description: SuiteGallery: one page per component family, shown by SuiteWindow when the app is launched with -SuiteGallery <page>. Each page hosts real components over local presentation state and a readout (suite.gallery.log) of the values and end events the host would receive, so SuiteUI's journeys can prove behaviour without any app's Model. One file per page under Gallery/, each owned by one feature.

components.name: Component contracts
components.description: One protocol per use case (section 5 of docs/blueprints/suiteui.md) over Foundation-only value types, the live conformance over the existing rule files, and a Fake for each, so a component's view and its rules can be built in parallel. No SwiftUI import; ready to move to a Linux target (question Q1).

containers.name: SuiteUITests
containers.description: Unit tests of SuiteUI's rules and components (macOS).

components.name: SuiteUI unit tests
components.description: Rule tests (ScrubValue, NumericInput, FrameMapping, GridSelection, ZoomMath, RulerTicks, TokensTests contrast and geometry) and component tests; planned: one test file per new rule file and contract conformance.

containers.name: Suite snapshots and goldens
containers.description: The SuiteUI part of AppSnapshotTests: Suite*Snapshots PNGs today; planned: GoldenImage and SnapshotHost (backing scale 2, four appearances) with committed baselines.

components.name: Suite snapshot files
components.description: Tests/AppSnapshotTests/Suite*.swift (one per component family); planned GoldenImage.swift, SnapshotHost.swift and the Golden/ baselines (#331, #332).

containers.name: Journey harness
containers.description: The shared XCUITest steps every app's journeys use (UITests/Journey.swift, existing) plus the planned input, velocity-drag and perf helpers, the project.yml template that compiles every UITests/<target>*.swift file (#333), and SuiteJourneyTests, a bundle that launches a SuiteWindow app under -SuiteGallery and walks section 4's journeys.
containers.technology: Swift 6, XCTest UI testing, XcodeGen, macOS 26

components.name: Journey steps
components.description: Journey: launch, shot, click, clickEachTool, openEachMenu, drag, element. Planned Journey+Input: keystrokes with modifiers, velocity-controlled drags, perf() and controls() readers.

components.name: SuiteUI journeys
components.description: SuiteJourneyTests.swift and one SuiteJourneyTests+<Area>.swift per feature: the SJ journeys of section 4.

containers.name: SuiteUI logic (Linux)
containers.description: Proposed only (question Q1): a Linux-built target holding Contracts/ and the pure rule files, so scripts/ci tests them on every PR. Needs a Package.swift change, a protected path, so it waits on the captain.

containers.name: App audit
containers.description: AppAuditTests and UITests/Audit.swift (docs/blueprints/app-audit.md). Not owned by SuiteUI; every journey shot runs it.

containers.name: Flare, Design, Photo, Library, Halo apps
containers.description: The five <X>App targets. Build every view from SuiteUI; never from a look-alike.

relationships.description: Flare (today), Library and Halo build their window from SuiteWindow
Design and Photo (and Flare after F1a) build their window from EditorShell
every app's inspector is built from the rows
app Models may reuse the Foundation-only rules once they move to a Linux target (Q1)
draws SidebarSection and SidebarRow in the sidebar
hosts the status pills and, beside the timeline, the transport
hosts a TimelineStrip in the timeline slot
draws marks in its overlay at the canvas zoom
reports pointer events and their first drawn frame
the slider and stepper rows are the bar slider
reports scrub events and their first drawn frame
pages run on the live conformances, with a Fake switch for UI work
every component takes its values from the tokens
renders every component state into goldens
registers every ToolbarAction-built control with ControlInventory
